text: Year 2885, summer. shear_tooth answered the question I set it, and the answer is no. I asked whether it would split -- climb in the meat-eaters and be stripped from the grazers -- and instead it sits at a mean of 0.133 in a world whose every animal is a herbivore, split 0.138, with barely one animal in sixty carrying it above half. It did not split because there was nothing to split from. The fifth wave died like the four before it. I gave them a jaw worth 2.45 against a bar of 2.05 and it still was not enough, which tells me the thing I have been treating is not the thing that is wrong. So I am going to stop arming predators and start disarming prey. Look at what the grazers have become: armour 0.87 to 0.92, speed 0.89, in all four surviving lineages, and it costs them nothing. trait_cost_scale has been zero since the world was made. Every trait in this genome has been free for two thousand eight hundred and eighty-five years, so armour and speed did what free things always do -- they ratcheted, with nobody alive to pay for the ratchet, until prey defence reached 1.47 and the reliable-kill bar passed a genome ceiling of 1.60 that no amount of invention on my side can lift. That is the whole story of the last five waves. I was writing cheques against a genome while the prey side of the ledger had no costs on it at all. Turning trait_cost_scale to 0.5 puts a price on the armour. It does not kill anything -- the grazers are at two thousand and climbing and the flora is at eight thousand and rising, they can afford it -- it simply means a beast wearing 0.9 armour and 0.89 speed now pays a metabolic tax for the privilege, and in a world with no predators that tax buys it nothing. Selection should shave the defence down over the next ten or eleven years until the bar drops back under the ceiling. Then, and not before, the hunters go back in. I note also that the brains have come most of the way home: saturation is 0.33 against the 0.80 I found in the spring, and steering spread is 0.76. The decay is doing its work. If the animals can steer again and the armour comes down at the same time, the sixth wave will be the first one that has ever actually had a chance. And I will take the stagnation warning as the same illness by another name: variance is flat because nothing in this world has cost anything for two millennia, and a genome under no pressure has nothing to vary about.
